claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser melting can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
The intervention produces a porous microstructure with an optimized pore size and distribution.
Controlled porosity reduces the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
An optimized porous structure retains sufficient load-bearing cross-sectional area to preserve mechanical strength.
Solid-solution strengthening is an inherent contributor to the mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr.
Lattice distortion is an inherent contributor to the mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr.
Solid-solution and lattice-distortion strengthening remain effective after controlled porosity is introduced.
SLM-induced controlled porosity will reduce density with only minimal loss of mechanical strength at room temperature.
SLM-induced controlled porosity will reduce density with only minimal loss of mechanical strength at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The proposed hypothesis applies from room temperature to 1000 °C.
The proposed hypothesis applies under both tensile and compressive loading.
The optimal porosity level and pore-size distribution are unknown and require experimental determination.
A tensile-strength loss greater than 20% at room temperature or elevated temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, whereas the predicted outcome permits a minimal loss and the rejection rule permits losses of up to 20% without falsification.
The stated scope includes tensile and compressive loading, but the proposed experiment measures only tensile behavior and therefore cannot test the compressive portion of the hypothesis.
